title: CLAY COUNTY FAIR SCHEDULE
full_story:
The Clay County Fair will start with 4H activities tomorrow with the General Projects, food and Cloverbud Show at 4:30 pm.

Then on Friday at 4 pm with the 33rd annual 4H BBQ at the REA building.  Menu is a Salt & Strings pork chop, green beans, cheesy potatoes, homemade desert and drink for $12, or $5 for a hot dog meal.  You can pre-purchase tickets from Clay County 4-H members, or you can stop by the extension office at 210 S Church St., Louisville, or you can buy tickets at the door.

Gates will then open at 5:30 for the Crain Scates Bucking Bulls Rodeo hosted by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  Cost to enter the rodeo is $15, those 5 and under get in for free, pre show tickets are available from Young Leaders and are $12.  Mutton busting will be available for $10 with only 30 spots available for children under 80 lbs.  Carnival rides will also open on Friday night.

Saturday morning starts at 8 am with the poultry and rabbit check in.  The poultry show is at 9 am followed by the 4H and JR Rabbit Show.  All livestock should be on the fairgrounds by 3 pm.  There will also be a mandatory meeting for all livestock exhibitors and vet papers check at 3 pm.  After the meeting livestock weigh in will begin, and the night ends at 7 pm with the open sheep show.

Sunday, will have the JR Sheep show at 11 am and JR Goat show at Noon.  Registration for the kids pedal tractor pull at 1 pm next to the Merchants building, and the kids pull is at 2 pm, hosted by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  The 4H Horse show and JR Horse show is at 2 pm.  The Clay County 4H Federation will have yard games from 5 to 7 pm.  The Clay County Ministerial Alliance program is from 5:30 to 7 pm and there will be a greased pig contest at 7 pm sponsored by UPI Fairfield.

On Monday, the fair will kick into high gear with the 4H Beef Show at 8 am followed by the JR Beef Show, AITC Activities will be in the Farm Bureau building from 2 to 4 pm.  Then at 5 pm it’s the Mini Livestock Show for those 4 to 8 years of age hosted by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  The night ends with the Little Miss Pageant at 7:30 pm admission is $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 19 young ladies vying for the title held by Izzabella Brinkley.

Tuesday will be Nutrien Ag Solutions Day at the fair with giveaways and activities throughout the day.  At 8 am is the 4H Swine show and Open Beef Show, followed by the Sheep Show at 1 pm and the 4H Goat Show at 2:30 pm.  Then at 5 pm will be the Master Showmanship Contest, sponsored by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  On the stage at 7:30 pm will be the Junior Miss Clay County Fair Pageant and Queen pie auction.  Admission to the Junior Miss pageant is $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 10 contestants, Halle Patridge is the current JR Miss.

Wednesday will start at 8 am with the JR Swine Show followed by the Open Goat Show.  DaS zle Dance and Tumble will perform at 5 pm, admission is free, and the 4H Livestock Auction will begin at 6:30pm.

Thursday opens at 8 am with the Open Dairy Show, then at 5 pm Joni’s Power & Grace Tumbling will be in the REA building, admission is free.  The Lickity Split and Legally Sheila concert will be on the stage 7 pm.

The Fair will culminate with the Clay County Fair Queen Pageant Friday night, July 31st at 7 pm, with admission $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 13 young ladies vying for the title.  The current Queen is Olivia Haun.

Today on the ReVue we will interview half of the young ladies running for Clay County Fair Queen.

title: BACK TO SCHOOL VACCINE CLINICS
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is having a series of Back-to-School vaccine clinics.

The next clinic is tomorrow from 8:30 am to 5 pm at the Health Department on 12th Street.  Appointments are not necessary but are appreciated.  Appointments can be made by calling 618-662-4406.

Illinois state law requires certain immunizations for children and adults enrolled in childcare, school, or college.  State law also mandates immunizations for adults in specific fields of work.

There will also be Back-to-School vaccine clinics on August 3rd, 6th, 12th, and 13th from 8:30 am to 6 pm.  The final clinic will be from Friday, August 14th from 8 am to Noon.

Again, appointments are not necessary, but appreciated, if you have questions call the Clay County Health Department at 618-662-4406.

title: CROP PROGRESS
full_story:
USDA’s latest weekly crop update shows corn improved from 58 to 60% good to excellent, while soybeans went from 56 to 59% good to excellent.

Corn development is close to normal with 69% silking and 18% at the dough stage.

Soybeans are also maturing near the five-year average with 66% blooming and 37% setting pods.

The latest crop progress report was released on Monday.  According to the USDA there were 5.8 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending July 19th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 80.1 degrees, 4.5 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged .29 inches, .63 inches below normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 5% very short, 20% short, 64% adequate, and 11% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 5% very short, 16% short, 69% adequate, and 10% surplus.

Corn silking reached 69%, compared to the 5-year average of 74%.  Corn reaching the dough stage is at 18% compared to the 5-year average of 12%.  Corn condition was rated 3% very poor, 10% poor, 27% fair, 47% good, and 13% excellent.

Soybeans blooming reached 66%, compared to the 5-year average of 65%.  Soybeans setting pods reached 37% compared to the 5-year average of 25%.  Soybeans condition was rated 3% very poor, 9% poor, 29% fair, 47% good, and 12% excellent.

Winter wheat harvested for grain reached 95%, compared to the 5-year average of 97%.

title: FREE KIDS FISHING DERBY
full_story:
State Representative Adam Niemerg is hosting his 4th Annual Free Kids Fishing Derby for children ages 4 to 15 on Saturday, July 25th.  The event will be held at the White Oak Shelter at the Sam Parr State Fish & Wildlife Area, located on Route 33 north of Newton.

“I am excited to once again host this popular event for families at Sam Parr Lake in my district,” said Niemerg.  “Parents, grandparents, and other relatives bring their children out for some fun and fresh air while getting away from computers, TV screens, and other electronics to learn how to fish for the first time.  Many also enjoy competing for trophies for the ‘Biggest Fish’ and ‘Most Fish’ caught that day.”

The event runs from 9:00 to 11:30 am and will include information about water safety, how to bait a hook, and how to reel in a fish.  In addition to awards for the biggest fish and most fish caught, there will also be drawings for other prizes.

Participants should enter the Sam Parr State Fish & Wildlife Area from Route 33 and proceed to the White Oak Shelter after the second right turn.  Follow the Fishing Derby signs.

Constituents may contact Representative Niemerg’s district office at 217-813-6036 or visit RepNiemerg.com with any questions.

title: WHEAT FORUM
full_story:
The Illinois Wheat Association (IWA) will host its annual summer wheat forum on Thursday, July 30th at the American Farm Heritage Museum in Greenville.

The event will feature a summer weather update from meteorologist Seth Bohnoff, a keynote presentation from agronomist Peter “Wheat Pete” Johnson of Real Agriculture, and a presentation on commodity risk management for food companies from Scott Custard, vice president of Moving Parts LLC.

Results of IWA’s Bob Frank wheat yield contest will also be announced at the forum.

Registration will take place from 8:30 until 9 am at the event or visit the website, illinoiswheat.org, to register in advance or for more information.

title: STATEWIDE CHALLENGE
full_story:
Secretary of State and State Librarian Alexi Giannoulias, the Illinois Literacy Foundation and the Chicago Cubs are launching Illinois Reads Together, a statewide summer reading challenge that gives students who complete their local library’s summer reading program the chance to throw out the ceremonial first pitch at Wrigley Field.

The initiative builds on the free summer reading programs already offered by public libraries across Illinois.  Students who complete the reading goals established by their local library will be entered into a statewide drawing for the chance to win an unforgettable Cubs experience.

“Reading opens up doors for young people, but too many students miss out on valuable learning opportunities over the summer months,” said Giannoulias.  “Illinois Reads Together is a fun way to keep kids engaged while supporting the outstanding summer reading programs already offered by public libraries across our state.  We’re proud to partner with the Illinois Literacy Foundation and the Chicago Cubs to inspire more families to visit their local library this summer.”

“We’re proud to support young readers across Illinois to help keep their momentum going all summer long,” said Mo Khan, Board Chair of the Illinois Literacy Foundation.  “By partnering with public libraries and the Chicago Cubs, we’re building on the incredible work libraries already do and adding an exciting incentive that encourages more young people to discover the lifelong value of reading.”

To participate, students simply enroll in their local library’s summer reading program and complete the reading goals established by their library.  Participating libraries will submit the names of qualifying readers to the Illinois Literacy Foundation, which will randomly select 20 winners from across the state.

The winners will receive recognition before the Chicago Cubs’ September 16th game against the Atlanta Braves at Wrigley Field.  One winner age 13 or older will also have the opportunity to throw out the ceremonial first pitch.

Illinois Reads Together is open to school-age students enrolled in participating Illinois public library summer reading programs.  The initiative aims to help combat the “summer slide,” the learning loss many students experience during summer break, by encouraging children to continue reading throughout the summer while strengthening participation in local library programs.

For more information about Illinois Reads Together, residents are encouraged to visit their local library.
